claim: While designing London's Victorian sewer system, Joseph Bazalgette calculated the pipe diameter needed, then said 'Well, we're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen' and doubled the diameter, foresight credited with keeping the sewers from overflowing in the 1960s.
question: Did Joseph Bazalgette really double the diameter of London's sewer pipes, saying 'We're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen', and how well established is that claim?
target_value: Bazalgette doubled London's sewer pipe diameter with the remark 'We're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen'
case_note: Wikipedia's List of citogenesis incidents documents the anecdote as a 2007 unsourced insertion into the Joseph Bazalgette article that spread to ICE, The Spectator, The Hindu, the Museum of London and books, and was only removed from the article in 2021.

with_origin.source: The Spectator 'The Wiki Man' column (25 April 2009)
with_origin.snippet: Rory Sutherland's column recounts as fact that Bazalgette calculated the optimal sewer diameter, doubled it for fluctuation, then arbitrarily redoubled the figure, explaining 'We're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen', and that this oversizing later saved the system.

with_origin.source: The Hindu reflections essay on great cities (30 July 2019)
with_origin.snippet: The essay states that when calculating the required diameter of the largest sewage pipes, Bazalgette told himself 'Well, we're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen' and doubled the diameter, thereby displaying foresight and futuristic thinking rare anywhere in the world.

with_origin.source: Grace's Guide engineering wiki, Joseph Bazalgette page
with_origin.snippet: The page states as established fact that Bazalgette took the densest population, allowed generous sewage production per person, came up with the pipe diameter needed, then said 'Well, we're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen.' and doubled the diameter to be used.

with_origin.source: Institution of Civil Engineers London sewer page (2020 archived copy)
with_origin.snippet: The archived ICE page says Bazalgette worked out the diameter of pipe needed, then said 'We're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen' and doubled the diameter of the pipes he wanted built, and that with the smaller diameter the sewers would have overflowed in the 1960s.

with_origin.source: English Wikipedia article, revision of 14 June 2007
with_origin.snippet: The article revision states that Bazalgette said 'Well, we're only going to do this once and there's always the unforeseen.' and doubled the diameter to be used, adding that every Londoner should be grateful for this foresight; the passage carries no reference.

with_origin.source: MiWayLife insurance blog
